messages.author: 7c2e44f7a6b9ca54
messages.subject: Opposite of melt but not cast?
parts:
In an SQL table I have payments and dates.

I am grouping them into monthly payments and get into a data frame which
looks like

month amount
1 2008-02 100.00
2 2008-03 100.00
3 2008-04 250.50
...
13 2009-01 100.00
14 2009-02 125.00
15 2009-03 130.50
16 2009-04 140.00
...
75 2014-05 300.00

I would like to plot the amounts for each month of every year in a
single graph in a different color.

So I reckon I need something like

2008 2009 2010 ... 2014
01 100.00
02 100.00 125.00
03 100.00 130.50
04 250.00 140.00
...
12

Any pointers on how I do this?

I know that there is no payment for January 2008, so if this an issue, a
pointer on how to add an amount of 0.00 would also be appreciated.

el

messages.author: bfc2eb6b71169017
messages.subject: Re: Opposite of melt but not cast?
parts:
I think you're good to go with your original data.frame. I would do something along the lines of

ggplot(my.df, aes(x = month, y = amount) + geom_point()

or whatever geom you want to use. It will probably help if you have 'month' in Date form (as.Date(x, format = "%Y-%m)).

Cheers,
Roman

messages.author: 373beb702917b8b5
messages.subject: Re: Opposite of melt but not cast?
parts:
Hi el,

I don't think the question is sufficiently clear, but my best guess is
that you're looking for something like this:


library(reshape2)
dat <- data.frame(
dat[-1],
colsplit(
dat$month,
pattern = "-",
names = c("year", "month"))
)

ggplot(dat,
aes(x = month,
y = amount,
color = factor(year))) +
geom_line()

Best,
Ista
